summary: Point Lepreau Lighthouse on the Bay of Fundy, New Brunswick: lit 1831, burned 1898, struck and destroyed 1956; the concrete octagon stands closed on Point Lepreau Generating Station grounds.

structures.note: Wooden octagonal tower (LighthouseFriends description, 1886); burned January 1898
Octagonal wooden tower in operation 1 October 1899; struck by lightning and destroyed December 1956
Octagonal, red and white horizontal bands (Coast Guard list). LighthouseFriends dates it 1958; Rowlett gives 1959
Frame fog-alarm building; enlarged for the diaphone c.1905; all other station buildings removed after 1980 (LighthouseFriends)
Keeper's dwelling at $5,975. The Marine report for the year ended 31 March 1922 records it; removed after 1980

access.note: Not accessible to the public (LighthouseFriends). Grounds and tower closed. Owned by the Canadian Coast Guard; the site lies on the grounds of the Point Lepreau Generating Station (New Brunswick Power is site manager). Visits may be arranged through the generating station.

events.note: Keeper's dwelling and lighthouse built; the commissioners were granted £500 in 1831 (LighthouseFriends)
Station established 1831; Pettingell paid as keeper from 1 September 1831
Lower light moved from the second floor to the ground floor, 28 feet from the upper light
Steam fog signal established; total cost $3,702 with engineer's dwelling and well
New lamps and 18- and 22-inch reflectors; light seen 24 miles to Head Harbour and north end of Grand Manan
New frame fog-alarm building on the point in front of the tower, $1,987, housing an improved Champion foghorn
Lower light discontinued in November 1886 because the fog-alarm building obscured it
Fire in January 1898 claimed the lighthouse, fog alarm and thirty tons of coal; temporary light from a mast
New octagonal wooden tower, Francis Cassidy, $1,325; in operation 1 October 1899; parts redone to pass inspection
Diaphone replaced the fog horn; building enlarged (Marine report for the year ended 30 June 1905; LighthouseFriends dates it 1905)
Diaphone blast changed (Marine report for the year ended 30 June 1906)
Inspected 18 September 1906; diaphone renewed; plant changed to run on low-pressure air
Triple flash reflector on the tower (LighthouseFriends)
New keeper's dwelling at $5,975. LighthouseFriends gives 1921; the Marine report for the year ended 31 March 1922 records it
Struck by lightning in December 1956 during a storm and totally destroyed (LighthouseFriends); the Lighthouse Directory says the wooden tower burned after the strike
Present octagonal concrete tower with red and white horizontal bands. LighthouseFriends: 1958; Rowlett: 1959
De-staffed in 1980; all other station buildings removed afterwards (LighthouseFriends)

corrections.why: The standing octagonal tower dates from after the December 1956 lightning. The 1831 tower burned in January 1898 (LighthouseFriends, Rowlett). The Coast Guard list gives the tower as 17.6 m. Dates for the concrete tower differ (1958 LighthouseFriends, 1959 Rowlett); the proposal uses LighthouseFriends' year, which the editor should confirm.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1831 is the station's first light (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett 'station established 1831'). The 1959 date (Rowlett) and 1958 (LighthouseFriends) are for the present concrete tower, which replaced the wooden tower of 1899 after the 1956 lightning. The first-year conflict in the record is between a first tower and the present one.

notes_for_editor: Pre-1900 history rests on LighthouseFriends, which summarises the Province of New Brunswick and Dominion records it cites; those records were not read directly, so the 1831, 1839 and 1848 facts are LighthouseFriends' account. The 1905, 1906, 1907 and 1922 Marine report passages were read in the corpus. Keeper names: the LighthouseFriends roster is the basis. The Marine keeper tables (1906, 1907 and 1909 volumes) print 'Belding, R. L' and 'Robert L. Belding' and the 1915 table prints 'W. Snider' (Sept. 9, 1914); these were matched by column position and are NOT used as evidence. Rowlett gives the light as a flash every 3 s; the Coast Guard list gives Fl W 5s; the record and the story use the Coast Guard list. Conflict left open: the concrete tower's year (1958 LighthouseFriends, 1959 Rowlett and Wikidata). LighthouseFriends' 1913 electric plant and 1918 reflector were not checked in the corpus (no 1913 or 1918 passage was matched). No 1898 newspaper report of the fire was found in Chronicling America. The Parks Canada heritage-lighthouse list cached on this machine had no match for Point Lepreau (the cache may be truncated). roster.py covers the United States only, so no USLHS roster was used for this Canadian station. The 1937-1944 keeper gap is in LighthouseFriends' roster.
